title: The Day the Snowbank Blinked
skyStory: March kicks the door open like a lion with wet paws. Up above, a last quarter moon sits in Sagittarius, half lit and fully restless, flipping through a travel brochure for a place called Spring. It keeps asking if we are there yet. Saturn says no. Mars says almost. The snowbank at the end of the driveway hears all this and blinks first.

reading: The cabin chimney is puffing in short, confident bursts this morning, which is cabin language for: you have more firewood than you think. Somewhere in your week there is a task you have been treating like a mountain. It is a molehill wearing a mountain costume. Pull the costume off before noon.

At 4:40 pm a door will stick, a lid will refuse, or a zipper will jam. Do not wrestle it. Breathe out, try once more gently, and it will give. The [[Knight of Pentacles]] is slow on purpose, and today he is trying to show you that slow and stuck are not the same animal. One of them is just warming up.
joel.mission: Find the oldest pencil in the house, sharpen it, and write tomorrow's top three tasks with it in your neatest handwriting.
joel.omen: A crow standing on a snowbank like it owns the deed. It means the hard part of winter has signed its resignation.
joel.elementWhy: the snowbank is still in charge

reading: The shore has gone quiet in that grey, listening way it gets before the ice starts thinking about leaving. You are in the same mood: watching, collecting, saying very little, noticing everything. The Wood Rat files away three useful facts before lunch without even trying.

Late in the afternoon someone will tell you a story badly. They will skip the best part and lead with the ending. You will feel your hands twitch, ready to fix it. Let them finish. Then ask one question that makes them tell the good part properly, and watch their face light up like a porch lamp. That is your level-up magic, and it works on everyone.
nancy.mission: Rename one ordinary object in your home with a grand title, like The Honourable Spatula, and use the title out loud all day.
nancy.omen: A puddle shaped like a map of somewhere you have never been. It means a small adventure is already on its way.
nancy.stoneWhy: the shore is thinking about thawing

together.text: First of the month, so declare it officially. Each of you send the other a one-line weather report for March written like a pirate captain at the helm. Bonus points for the word scallywag. The best report gets pinned to the fridge of the imagination for thirty-one days.

title: The Mountain Hosts a Tea Party
skyStory: The waning crescent moon slips into Capricorn and knocks politely on Nancy's mountain door. Saturn answers in slippers, delighted, and puts the kettle on. They are deciding which winter habits get to stay for spring. The list is short and very well organized. Mars was not invited and is sulking on the porch, eating the decorative pinecones out of spite.

reading: The moon is visiting Nancy's sign, so you are a guest in someone else's weather today. Guests do not rearrange the furniture. Your instinct will be to fix, steer, and improve three things you were not asked about. Keep the paws folded. The Tiger can admire a well-run house without redecorating it.

Around 11:15 am a quiet person in a meeting or a message will say something smarter than anything else said all day. Point at it out loud. Give them the credit, name them the hero, then step back. Words are your gift, Life Path 3, and the best use of them today is turning a spotlight around and aiming it at somebody else.
joel.mission: Compliment a stranger's choice of hat, scarf or mittens with the seriousness of a museum curator describing a priceless painting.
joel.omen: A mug with a chip on the rim. It means something imperfect is about to turn out to be your favourite.
joel.stoneWhy: clear and bright, like a guest

reading: Capricorn moon, and the mountain is hosting today. You will feel unusually in charge today, but the cozy kind of in charge, like a lighthouse keeper with excellent biscuits. Things you organize this morning will stay organized for weeks. Saturn guarantees it in writing.

There is a drawer, folder or inbox that has been quietly judging you since January. Today you can beat it in under twenty minutes. Set a timer. Hum while you work. The [[Six of Swords]] says some crossings are big and slow and some are just carrying old receipts to the recycling bin. Both count. Both make the boat lighter for the long row ahead.
nancy.mission: Set a twenty-minute timer and tidy one small space while narrating it like a nature documentary about a very clever rat.
nancy.omen: Steam rising off a warm cup in a perfect spiral. It means your plans this week are lined up better than you realize.

together.text: Make a cup of something warm at the same hour tonight, wherever you each are, and raise it toward the other's direction. Say one sentence about something winter taught you. Saturn is listening and will file both answers under Good Lessons, Keep Forever.

title: The Day of the Second Mitten
skyStory: A slim waning crescent lingers in Capricorn, thinner today, like a moon that has eaten most of its own sandwich and is saving the crust for later. Saturn approves of the restraint. The wind outside is doing that March thing where it pretends to be warm and then bites. Every lost mitten in town feels a strange pull, as if something is about to come home.

reading: Patience is not your favourite flavour, but today it comes with sprinkles. Something you have been waiting on will not arrive yet, and that is good news in disguise. The extra time lets you notice a better version of the plan, hiding in the margin like a doodle you forgot you drew.

Late afternoon brings a small, odd gift: a found object, a returned item, a message from someone you thought had forgotten. Receive it without explaining why you do not deserve it. The [[Six of Pentacles]] is holding out a cup. Your only job is to take it and say thank you, full stop, no footnotes, no offer to repay it by Thursday.
joel.mission: When anyone thanks you today, answer only with the words you are welcome, and resist adding anything else at all.
joel.omen: A single mitten perched on a fence post. It means something you misplaced is about to find its way back to you.

reading: The moon is still lounging in your sign, so you get one more day of home advantage. Use it to say no to something small. Not dramatically. Just a pleasant, firm no, the kind a mountain gives to a cloud that wants to sit on it all day.

Your diamonds catch a stray beam of light around 2 pm and throw a little rainbow on the wall. Take this as a memo from the wind element: you are allowed to change direction without a reason. Try a different route home, a different chair, a different mug. The Wood Rat in you will spot something new in the changed view, something everybody else walks past daily.
nancy.mission: Take a totally different route somewhere routine and name one new thing you notice along the way, out loud, to nobody.
nancy.omen: A rainbow on the wall from a ring or a window. It means your hunch about something this week is correct.

together.text: Five words each, no more: the thing you are waiting on this month, sent to the other with zero explanation. Let the other person hold those five words, like a pebble in a pocket, until the thing finally arrives.

title: The Day of Two Identical Hats
skyStory: The crescent moon has drifted into Aquarius and is wearing a lab coat now, scribbling equations about probability on the clouds. Thirteen percent lit and fully nerdy. Uranus slides it a note: run the experiment on those two. The moon grins, flips a cosmic coin, and arranges for the same ridiculous object to cross both of their paths before supper. The coin lands on its edge.

reading: Something very specific is coming: a knitted hat with an absurdly large orange pompom. You will see it on a stranger, a sign, or a screen, probably around 1:30 pm. Take note of where. This is not random. The moon is conducting an experiment and you are the control group.

Here is the twist. Nancy is getting the same hat in her day. When you compare notes tonight, you will both say the same word at once. Do not even scream. It is the universe showing off its sense of humour and reminding you that the thread between the cabin and the shore is real, thick, and occasionally wears a pompom.
joel.mission: Text Nancy a single emoji tonight that describes the strangest thing you saw today, then wait for hers before saying anything.
joel.omen: An orange pompom, anywhere. It means the moon is running tests and you have passed the first one.

reading: Your intuition is set to maximum today, Life Path 11. You will know who is calling before you look, guess the next song before it plays, and possibly predict what someone orders at a counter. Do not tell anyone. Just smile like the wise old Wood Rat you are.

Then the big one: an orange pompom, ridiculous and proud, will cross your path in the afternoon. Joel is being sent the same one. When you find out, the correct response is ΔΕΣ, said with your hands as large as possible. The [[Wheel of Fortune]] does not spin for nothing, and today it spun specifically to make you both laugh at the same time.
nancy.mission: Guess three small things before they happen today, like the colour of the next car, and keep secret score on your hand.
nancy.omen: The same number on two receipts or clocks. It means your intuition is right on schedule, so trust your next hunch.
nancy.stoneWhy: his stone hears the joke too

together.text: Tonight, compare days. Somewhere in there is an orange pompom, and when you both find it, say DES out loud together on the count of three. Then write down the time it happened. The universe likes to know its jokes landed.

title: The Inventory of Small Wins
skyStory: The waning crescent is down to a fingernail clipping of light in Aquarius, seven percent and fading. The moon is doing its end-of-cycle bookkeeping, counting every little victory from the past month on an abacus made of stars. Saturn checks the math twice. Mars just wants to know if any of the wins were loud. The answer is no, and that is exactly the point.

reading: The cabin is doing inventory tonight: kindling stacked, kettle filled, boots by the door. You need the same pause. You have finished more this past month than you give yourself credit for, and the list is hiding because you never stop long enough to read it.

Before dinner, write down five things you did since February. Small counts. Fixed a hinge counts. Answered a hard message counts. Made someone laugh in a dull meeting definitely counts. The [[Nine of Cups]] in its shadow form whispers that wishes feel hollow when you never notice them coming true. Notice them. Read the list back once, slowly, like it belongs to someone you admire.
joel.mission: Write five small wins from the past month on a sticky note and put it where you will see it tomorrow morning.
joel.omen: A neatly stacked pile of anything, like plates, wood or books. It means your foundations are stronger than they feel.

reading: The Wood Rat is a famous collector, and today you are collecting proof. Proof that the steady, patient work has been working. It has. Someone you helped level up recently is about to tell you so, maybe sideways, maybe as a joke, but it counts.

Your diamond catches the light from a computer screen at 3:20 pm and you will remember, suddenly, something good you said to someone weeks ago. It landed. It mattered. The heart element wants you to sit with that for a full sixty seconds without rushing to the next task. Sixty seconds. Count them on your fingers if you have to. Your hands love a job.
nancy.mission: Spend sixty uninterrupted seconds remembering one person you helped this winter, then send them a short hello with no reason given.
nancy.omen: A paper clip, ribbon or thread found on the floor. Some untidy little matter is about to wrap itself up with a bow.
nancy.elementWhy: feel the wins, not just list

together.text: Trade lists. Each of you send the other your three proudest small wins of the past month. The other person must respond with one word only, something huge, like magnificent or legendary or historic. Both lists get stored in the cabin's imaginary trophy case.

title: New Moon, Blank Page
skyStory: The new moon arrives in Aquarius, three percent lit and basically invisible, like a page fresh out of the package. Uranus hands it a fountain pen. The sky holds its breath. Whatever gets written tonight becomes the first sentence of a whole new chapter, so the stars are leaning in close, hoping it is something with a good opening line and maybe a dragon.

reading: Ten things are tugging at your sleeve, and the new moon only has room for one. The [[Knight of Wands]] is pacing beside you with a torch, asking which way to aim. You know the answer already. You knew it in the shower this morning. Say it out loud.

Write that one thing on a fresh page. Not a list. One line. Then tuck the page somewhere you will forget about it until the full moon on your birthday. When it comes back around, you will be surprised how far the Tiger carried it. Fire is fastest when it has one log to burn, not ten. Feed one log tonight.
joel.mission: Write a single sentence about the one thing you want this month and hide the page inside a book until March 21.
joel.omen: A candle or burner flame that leans one way. It means your chosen direction has the wind behind it.

reading: The tide is out under this dark moon, and the beach is all fresh sand and possibility. The shore is ready for new footprints. Yours have a destination in mind; you have been walking toward it for a while, steady as the mountain, quiet as the snow.

Tonight, write down the next small step, not the whole map. One stone to step on. The [[Six of Swords]] reminds you the crossing is still underway, and that the boat moves best with a clear point on the far shore. Pick the point. Joel is rowing too, even when you cannot see the oar. The water carries both of you.
nancy.mission: Draw a tiny map with just two dots on it: where you are and where you are heading next, then stick it somewhere secret.
nancy.omen: Footprints in fresh snow or mud going the same direction as you. It means someone has already cleared part of your path.

together.text: Under the new moon, swap your one-line intentions for the month. Do not comment. Do not advise. Just reply with a single flame emoji to say I saw it and I am holding it too. Check back on the full moon.

title: The Day the Fog Kept Secrets
skyStory: The moon is new and dark and has swum into Pisces, where everything gets soft around the edges. A thick sea fog rolls in off the water to match. Neptune drapes it over the treetops like a blanket over a birdcage. Shh, says the sky. Not everything has to be figured out today. Some secrets are just naps wearing a mysterious hat.

reading: The fog has wrapped the cabin so snugly that even the chimney smoke seems to be whispering. This is a day to move at half speed and enjoy it. If you feel guilty about resting, notice the guilt, wave at it, and keep resting anyway.

The [[Eight of Swords]] shows up as a reminder that the cage is often built from thoughts, not bars. Today you might feel stuck on a decision that does not need deciding yet. Here is the trick: put it in a box labelled Thursday and close the lid. Make a warm drink instead. Watch the fog move. It is moving very slowly, and so are you, and both of you are fine.
joel.mission: Take a fifteen-minute pause with no screen at all and just watch something move slowly, like clouds, fog, or snow.
joel.omen: A foghorn, a distant train, or a long low hum. It means you can stop listening for alarms and rest.
joel.stoneWhy: soft light for a soft day
joel.elementWhy: fog is water taking a nap

reading: Pisces is the dreamiest sign, and with the moon hiding inside it, your dreams last night were probably strange. A door that opened onto a beach. A cat that laughs like a kettle. A library made of seashells. Write down whatever you remember before it melts.

Somewhere in that dream is a clue. Not a prediction, a clue: a colour, a word, a feeling that keeps tugging. Life Path 11 means your dreams are not just dreams, they are drafts. Read yours over lunch. Circle one detail. By evening, you will understand what it was pointing at, probably while doing something boring, like folding socks.
nancy.mission: Write down one detail from last night's dream on a napkin or paper scrap and carry it in your pocket all day.
nancy.omen: A seashell, real or printed, in an unexpected place. It means a dream is trying to tell you something sweet.

together.text: Fog day rules: no big plans. Tonight each of you send the other the strangest dream image you can remember from this winter. The other person must invent its secret meaning, as dramatically and wrongly as possible. Accuracy is not invited.

title: The Darkest Little Sky
skyStory: Zero percent. The new moon in Pisces is fully hidden, the darkest night of the cycle, and the stars take full advantage, coming out in their best outfits. Orion is wearing a belt with extra sparkle. Without the moon to boss them around, the constellations are throwing a quiet party. It is a good night to let go of something and watch it float off into the dark.

reading: There is something heavy you have been carrying since February. Maybe a grudge against a printer. Maybe a promise you made to yourself that does not fit anymore. Tonight, under the darkest sky of the month, you are allowed to set it down.

Go outside, if the wind allows, and look up for one full minute. Find the brightest star you can. Tell it, silently, the thing you are letting go. Then turn around and walk back to the warm cabin without looking back, like a hero in a film walking away from a grand finale of fireworks. The [[Death]] card is not scary. It just means one chapter ends so the next can begin.
joel.mission: Step outside tonight, find the brightest star, and silently hand it one thing you are done carrying.
joel.omen: A star that seems to twinkle twice as fast as the others. It means the universe heard you and said got it.

reading: The Wood Rat is a famously excellent judge of what to keep and what to toss. Tonight you get to apply that talent to something invisible: an old worry, a story you have been telling yourself, a should that belongs to somebody else.

Write it on a scrap of paper. Then fold it into the smallest possible square, as small as your fingers can manage. Put it in a drawer you never open, or in the recycling. As the moon starts growing again tomorrow, so does the space where that worry used to be. You will notice the room by Friday. Saturn has already measured it and approves.
nancy.mission: Fold one worry written on paper into the smallest square you can manage, then hide it somewhere you never look.
nancy.omen: A clear night sky, even for a moment between clouds. It means the path ahead is clearer than you think.
nancy.elementWhy: bury the worry, plant the space

together.text: Darkest night of the month. Both of you name, privately, one thing to release. Then send each other a single star emoji at exactly 9 pm. The stars are watching the clock, and they love a synchronized ritual.

title: The Moon Knocks on the Tiger's Door
skyStory: The new moon crosses into Aries, two percent lit and already pacing. It has arrived in Joel's sign and immediately starts rearranging the furniture. Mars, ruler of Aries, flings open the door with both arms. Finally, someone with energy. They high-five so hard a comet changes lanes. Saturn, watching from the mountain, quietly hides the good china.

reading: The moon is in your house now, and it brought snacks and a megaphone. Expect to feel like starting things. Lots of things. You may feel a strong urge to announce a new project to everyone you meet. Pick one person. Tell only them.

Courage comes easily under an Aries moon, so spend it on something brave but small: the email you keep rewriting, the question you swallowed in last week's meeting, the shelf you meant to hang in January. The [[The Chariot]] is not in the official spread, but it showed up anyway, wheels spinning, ready to go. Point it at one thing and let the Tiger drive.
joel.mission: Send the message you have been rewriting in your head for days, exactly as it is right now, typos and all.
joel.omen: A red door, a red car or a red scarf before noon. It means the moon has your back in your own sign.
joel.stoneWhy: her stone holds your fire steady

reading: The moon has gone off to visit Joel's sign, which means the energy around you is suddenly very bouncy. People will interrupt more. Phones will ping more. The Wood Rat finds a high branch and watches the circus with an amused face.

Your ruby, Joel's stone, will feel especially warm on your pinky today, like it knows the moon is visiting home. Let a little of that Aries fire borrow your hands. Say yes to one bold, tiny thing: wearing the louder sweater, telling the story with the bigger finish, taking the seat at the front instead of the back. The mountain can be loud for an afternoon. It will still be a mountain tomorrow.
nancy.mission: Choose the bolder option on one small choice today, like a brighter colour or the front seat, and own it completely.
nancy.omen: A ram, a goat, or anything with horns on a sign or screen. It means borrowed fire is working in your favour.

together.text: Aries moon dare: each of you do one thing today that makes your heart beat a little faster, nothing risky, just brave. Report back tonight with a single sentence that starts with the words I actually did it.

title: The Day of Ten Unfinished Things
skyStory: A sliver of waxing crescent glows in Aries, six percent lit and full of plans. The moon has made a list. Then a list of lists. Then a vision board. Mars cheers it on from the sidelines with a foam finger. Saturn appears at the edge of the frame holding a single sticky note that reads, in very small letters, finish one.

reading: Let us be honest: there are at least ten unfinished projects in your orbit right now, circling like moons. Under this Aries crescent, an eleventh will try to join. Do not let it in. Bar the door politely. Hand it a pamphlet. Tell it to come back in April.

Instead, pick the unfinished thing closest to done and finish it today. Even if it is tiny. Even if it is boring. The [[Knight of Wands]] says the fire burns brightest when aimed, and the Tiger knows that crossing a finish line, any finish line, feels better than sprinting toward eleven. Victory lap at 5 pm. Mandatory.
joel.mission: Finish the single nearest-to-done project on your list today and do a small victory lap around the room when it is complete.
joel.omen: A shoelace coming untied. It means slow down for ten seconds and choose the one thing that matters.

reading: The shore is changing shape this week. The ice along the edge is going thin and grey, and you can hear it creak in the afternoon sun. Something in your own work is shifting too, from planning into doing. You can feel the click.

At 10:10 am, which is an extremely powerful time, glance at whatever you are working on and ask: what is the next tiny piece? Then do just that piece. Your patience has built the boat, the [[Six of Swords]] has the oars ready, and today the water finally starts moving under the hull. You may notice your hands telling the story of it before you have the words.
nancy.mission: At exactly 10:10 am, pause and name out loud the very next small step in your current project.
nancy.omen: Ice cracking or dripping from a roof edge. It means a long wait is ending, and movement starts now.

together.text: Each of you send the other your one-thing-to-finish today before 9 am. At 9 pm, report back with either a checkmark or a sad trombone noise typed out in words. No judgement either way. Trombones are noble instruments.

title: The Day the Kettle Refused
skyStory: The waxing crescent, eleven percent lit, is still bouncing around Aries like a kid on a trampoline. It has decided today is for pranks. Not mean ones. Just small mischief: a kettle that takes forever, a sock that vanishes, a word you cannot remember. Mars thinks this is hilarious. Saturn is writing a strongly worded letter to the management.

reading: Something in the kitchen will refuse to cooperate this morning. The kettle, the toaster, the drawer that sticks. The moon is testing your sense of humour. Pass the test by laughing out loud, even if you are alone. Especially if you are alone.

Midday brings a funny coincidence of words: you will think of a word just before someone says it. Write it down. It is your word of the day. Use it three times in conversation before dinner, as naturally as possible. If anyone notices, tell them the Aries moon made you do it. They will nod, because nobody argues with the moon, and the cabin will chuckle quietly to itself.
joel.mission: Pick an unusual word like flummox and slip it into three separate conversations before dinner without anyone catching on.
joel.omen: A sock without its partner sock in the laundry. It means a small mystery is about to solve itself cheerfully.

reading: The Wood Rat smells mischief on the breeze and decides to join in rather than fight it. Today you get to be the gentle trickster: hide a small, kind surprise for someone to find later. A note in a coat pocket. A drawing on a fogged mirror.

Around 2:45 pm, a coworker or a neighbour will say something so oddly specific that you will wonder if they have been reading your diary. They have not. The moon simply tapped them on the shoulder and whispered your thought into their ear as a joke. Laugh. Tell them, they are correct. Leave it at that, mysterious and smiling, like a rat in a wizard hat.
nancy.mission: Leave a small hidden note of kindness somewhere for someone to find later, then walk away whistling like nothing happened.
nancy.omen: Writing appearing on a foggy window or mirror. It means someone is thinking about you warmly right now.

together.text: Send each other the most dramatic possible description of one small inconvenience from today, written like an epic poem. The kettle took four minutes becomes a saga. The winner is whoever makes the other one snort first.

title: The Day Everyone Said Periwinkle
skyStory: The waxing crescent glides into Taurus, nineteen percent lit and suddenly very relaxed. Venus greets it with a soft blanket and a bowl of something warm. The moon, still a little giddy from Aries, decides to pull one last stunt before settling down. It picks a word, a strange and lovely word, and plants it in two places at once.

reading: Today a very unusual word is going to follow you around: periwinkle. You will hear it, read it, or see it written somewhere unexpected, probably before noon. It might be a paint colour, a shell, or a stranger saying it for no reason at all.

Then Nancy will text you, unprompted, with the exact same word. Do not even scream. That is the moon's last little Aries trick before it settles into Taurus and goes quiet. The [[The Star]] card would say this is proof the universe pays attention to small details, especially the ones you two share. Keep a list of these coincidences this year. It is going to be a long list.
joel.mission: Write down every strange coincidence today in a small notebook, and title the notebook Evidence in big letters.
joel.omen: Anything periwinkle blue. It means the cosmic link between cabin and shore is humming especially loudly today.

reading: A periwinkle is a little snail that lives along the shore, which is your territory, so of course the word comes to you first. You might find a shell, or hear someone say it, or spot the colour on a sign. Pay attention around 11:30 am.

Once you notice it, the urge to text Joel will be very strong. Do it. Type the word and nothing else. His reply will make you put your phone down and stare at the wall for a second. ΔΕΣ. The Wood Rat sees what others miss, and today what she sees is that coincidence is just the universe winking at you from across the bay.
nancy.mission: Text Joel a single word today with no context at all, and see if he understands it immediately.
nancy.omen: A small snail shell on a windowsill or path. It means two people are thinking the same thought right now.
nancy.stoneWhy: a clear signal across the water

together.text: The word of the day is periwinkle, and the universe has decided you both need to hear it. When it happens, text the other just DES, nothing more. Tonight, take turns guessing what colour the next surprise will be.

title: Sap Is Running, So Are We
skyStory: The crescent moon swells to twenty-eight percent in Taurus, the sign of comfort and good things slowly made. Down in the hardwoods, the maple sap has started to run, drip by drip into metal pails. Venus counts every drop with deep satisfaction. The moon leans in to smell the steam rising off the sugar shacks and sighs. Sweetness takes time, it says. Lots of time.

reading: It takes about forty buckets of sap to make one bucket of syrup, and that is the whole lesson for today. Your best work is not quick. It is boiled down, slowly, until only the good part remains. Stop rushing the pot.

The cabin wants you to do one thing the slow way today: hand-write a note, cook something that simmers, fix a thing properly instead of taping it. The [[Knight of Pentacles]] reversed has been teaching you that slowness is not a punishment. It is the recipe. By late afternoon you will taste the difference, and the Tiger will lie by the stove looking extremely pleased with itself.
joel.mission: Do one task today deliberately slowly, the old-fashioned way, from start to finish without checking your phone even once.
joel.omen: Steam rising from a pot, puddle or roof in sunshine. It means something you have been patient with is nearly ready.

reading: Taurus energy suits you: steady, earthy, and in no particular hurry. Today you will feel like making something cozy happen, a slow lunch, a warm room, an afternoon with nowhere to be. Follow the feeling. The Wood Rat has earned a nest day.

Somewhere in the afternoon a smell will hit you, woodsmoke, maple, or warm bread, and bring back a memory so vivid it feels like time travel. Let it. Tell somebody the story, with full hand choreography. Your storytelling magic works best when it starts from a sense like smell. People will lean in. Even the moon leans in, all twenty-eight percent of it.
nancy.mission: Tell one person a story today that begins with the phrase this smell reminds me of, and use both hands.
nancy.omen: The scent of woodsmoke drifting from nowhere in particular. It means a happy memory is about to become useful again.

together.text: Sugar season is here. Each of you describe to the other, in loving detail, the best warm thing you have ever smelled cooking. Make it rich and slow, like the sap. The listener must respond only with a long, satisfied mmm.

title: The Day Somebody Stole an Hour
skyStory: Overnight, the clocks sprang forward and an entire hour vanished into the sky. The first quarter moon, half lit in Gemini, is the prime suspect. It has two faces and an alibi for each one. Mercury, Gemini's ruler, is clearly in on it, whistling and juggling sixty stolen minutes behind its back. Somewhere a rooster is extremely confused. So is everyone.

reading: You are going to feel like you woke up in the wrong time zone. Lean into it. Today is a bit topsy-turvy anyway: daylight lingers longer, the evening feels stretched, and the moon is half lit and half plotting. It is also Pi Day, so circles are lucky.

Your mission is to find the missing hour. It is hiding somewhere in your day as a pocket of free time you did not expect, maybe twenty minutes, maybe forty. When you find it, do not fill it with work. Fill it with something round and joyful. A walk in a loop. A spin on a chair. A circle drawn freehand, perfectly, on the first try. Round things win today.
joel.mission: Draw the most perfect circle you can, freehand, in one go, and send a photo of it to Nancy as proof.
joel.omen: A clock still showing the old time somewhere. It means you have more time than you think today.
joel.elementWhy: Gemini moon blows the clocks around

reading: Gemini moons make everyone talk twice as much and listen half as well. You will be the exception. Today the Wood Rat listens to both sides of a conversation and spots the one sentence that solves everything. Say it quietly. Watch the room go oh.

Evening brings the first long, late daylight of the year. At around 6:30 pm, go to a window and notice: it is still bright. That light is your light, the light returning, the thing you were born on the solstice to promise. Stand in it for a moment, warm your pinky ruby in it, and know you kept your word to the world again this year.
nancy.mission: At 6:30 pm, find a window and stand in the late light for one full minute, ruby turned toward the sun.
nancy.omen: Sunlight on a wall long after it used to be dark. It means the light returning is returning just for you.

together.text: Pi Day plus the stolen hour. Each of you send the other a circle drawn freehand. The better circle wins the missing hour, which must then be spent on something gloriously unproductive. Mercury will judge, badly, and probably fudge the scores.

title: The Ides of Slightly Different Opinions
skyStory: The Ides of March arrive with a first quarter moon in Gemini, exactly half lit and arguing with itself about which half is better. Mercury moderates the debate badly. The light side says go. The dark side says wait. Both are right, which is very annoying. Somewhere a pair of mittens is having the same argument.

reading: You will hear two good opinions today that completely contradict each other, and you will want to pick a side immediately. The Tiger likes to pounce. But the half-lit moon suggests a different move: wait until tomorrow morning. The right answer is shy and arrives late.

This is a patience day disguised as a decision day. The [[Two of Swords]] sits blindfolded in your path, balancing both choices without dropping either. You do not have to choose yet. Put both options in an imaginary jar and give the jar a shake before bed. Look at it again over breakfast. The answer will float to the top by itself, like a cork.
joel.mission: Postpone one non-urgent decision until tomorrow morning and write the two options on separate pieces of paper.
joel.omen: Two birds arguing on a branch. It means both sides of your question have merit, so do not rush.

reading: Patience is your native language, so today is a good one for you. While everyone else flaps around making Ides of March jokes, you will move steadily through the day like the tide, getting exactly where you are going without needing anyone to notice.

Around 3 pm, someone will ask your opinion on something with two sides. Give them a third option they had not considered. The Wood Rat has a gift for finding the hidden door in a room with two obvious exits. They will look at you like you just pulled a coin from their ear. Smile serenely. Say nothing more.
nancy.mission: When someone offers you two choices today, propose a third option, even if it is silly, just to see what happens.
nancy.omen: A path that forks in the snow or mud. It means there is a third way, and you will see it first.
nancy.stoneWhy: layers show more than two sides

together.text: Gemini debate night. Pick a deeply silly topic, like whether pancakes are just flat cake, and argue opposite sides for five texts each. Then switch sides and argue the other way. Nobody wins. Everybody laughs. Mercury takes notes for future reference.

title: The Shell and the Chimney
skyStory: The first quarter moon steps into Cancer, sixty-one percent lit, and immediately wants to go home. Cancer is the crab sign, the homebody, the one who carries its house on its back. The moon finds a cozy shell and settles in. Down on Earth, every chimney gets a little extra smoke and every porch light switches on a few minutes earlier than usual.

reading: The cabin is calling you home today, in every sense. You might find yourself drawn to old photos, familiar music, a favourite worn-out sweater. Go with it. A Cancer moon is a reminder that the place you come back to matters as much as the places you go.

In the evening, do one small thing to make your space feel more like the cabin in your head. A lamp in a new spot. A candle. A blanket on the couch arranged just so. The Tiger, it turns out, also loves a warm den. Let yourself sink into it without a list or a plan. Receiving comfort is still receiving. It still counts.
joel.mission: Move one lamp, candle or blanket to make your home feel more like a cabin, then sit in that spot for ten minutes.
joel.omen: A porch light on in daylight. It means home is waiting for you, warm and ready, whenever you need it.

reading: The crab is a shore creature, and today the moon has moved into its sign, so your territory feels especially strong. You will want to tidy your nest, call someone you love, or simply sit by the water if the weather lets you. All three are correct.

Late afternoon, a memory will float up of a place where you felt completely safe. Maybe a kitchen. Maybe a beach. Maybe a room with a particular smell. Tell Joel about it tonight in three sentences. The [[Ten of Cups]] is not in your spread, but it wanders in today with a blanket and a cup of tea, saying home is a feeling you can carry.
nancy.mission: Describe your safest childhood place to Joel tonight in exactly three sentences, no more, no less.
nancy.omen: A crab, shell or anchor on a sign or label. It means you are carrying home with you everywhere today.

together.text: Cancer moon homecoming. Each of you describe one room from your childhood in three sentences. The other must guess one object that was definitely in that room. Correct guesses earn a cosmic gold star. Wrong guesses earn a story.

title: The Day of Unreasonable Green
skyStory: A waxing gibbous moon, seventy-two percent lit, floats in Cancer and squints at the town below, which has turned alarmingly green overnight. Green hats. Green scarves. A green dog, somehow. The moon is not sure what holiday this is, but it loves a party and decides to glow a little brighter in solidarity. Jupiter, always up for fun, starts a fiddle tune.

reading: Today rewards anyone brave enough to wear something completely ridiculous. Not subtle green. Unreasonable green. The Tiger looks magnificent in it, obviously, and the moon is watching from Cancer, ready to applaud the commitment.

Midafternoon, someone will start telling a story and lose the thread halfway through. Jump in and finish it for them, gloriously, with a much better ending than they planned. Life Path 3 was made for exactly this. The room will laugh. The storyteller will laugh hardest. Then hand the spotlight right back with a bow, like a fiddler passing the tune to the next player.
joel.mission: Wear the most unreasonably green item you own and, when complimented, claim it was a gift from the moon.
joel.omen: A four-leaf clover, real or drawn. It means luck is following you around today like a friendly golden retriever.

reading: There is a fiddle tune somewhere in your day, and your hands will find the rhythm before your brain does. The Wood Rat is a secret dancer. Let her out, even if it is only a little shuffle in the kitchen while the kettle boils.

Late in the day, someone you have helped will mention, out of the blue, that they are doing much better at something because of you. You will try to deflect. Do not. Say thank you, and then tell them one specific thing you noticed about how hard they worked. The [[Three of Cups]] is raising a glass in your honour. Clink it back.
nancy.mission: Do a ten-second kitchen jig while the kettle boils, then pour your drink with a dramatic flourish.
nancy.omen: A rainbow, painted or real. It means a happy surprise is waiting at the end of today, not tomorrow.

together.text: Unreasonable green day. Each of you photograph the greenest thing you see before sundown and send it over. The winner earns the right to name the next fog bank that rolls in. It must be named something gloriously fancy.

title: The Lion Wants a Microphone
skyStory: The waxing gibbous moon bounds into Leo, eighty-two percent lit and absolutely refusing to be ignored. Leo is the sign of the stage, the spotlight, the dramatic entrance. The moon has demanded a microphone and is now giving a speech about itself to the entire solar system. The Sun, Leo's ruler, is proud but also slightly embarrassed. Mars is in the front row, cheering.

reading: Leo moon, fire sign, and you are Life Path 3, the communicator. Today your words carry farther than usual. A sentence you say casually in the morning will get repeated by someone else by evening. Choose your casual sentences wisely. Make at least one of them kind.

Somewhere this week there is a presentation, a toast, a message or a pitch. Today is the day to rehearse it out loud, in the shower or the car, with full lion energy. The [[King of Wands]] is in the audience nodding along. You do not need to be perfect. You need to be you, at full volume, aimed at one point.
joel.mission: Rehearse something you need to say this week, out loud, with full dramatic gestures, at least twice.
joel.omen: A lion, cat or golden-haired dog staring at you. It means your voice is especially powerful today, so use it well.

reading: Leo moons push quiet people into the spotlight whether they asked or not. Today you may be called on unexpectedly to share an idea, a story or an opinion. You are ready. You have been ready for weeks. The Wood Rat has notes.

When it happens, tell it as a story, not a summary. Your hands will do the work. Start with a small detail, let it build, give it a twist at the end. People remember stories, not bullet points. By evening someone will quote you back to yourself, and you will realize your words went farther than you thought.
nancy.mission: Turn one ordinary update today into a small story with a beginning, a twist, and a satisfying ending.
nancy.omen: A spotlight, stage or bright shaft of sun through clouds. It means it is your turn to shine, even briefly.

together.text: Leo moon open mic. Each of you send the other a thirty-second voice memo telling a true story from this week in the most dramatic narration possible. The listener must applaud audibly. Standing ovations are encouraged and absolutely unchecked.

title: The Applause for Nobody in Particular
skyStory: The gibbous moon, ninety percent lit, is still basking in Leo, almost full and very aware of it. It has started signing autographs for passing comets. Spring is two days away and the moon is warming up for its big performance on Joel's birthday. Somewhere a snowdrop has pushed through the mud and is bowing to an empty theatre.

reading: Two days from your birthday, the universe starts dropping hints. A song you love on the radio. A stranger holding a door. A warm breeze where there should be cold. Each one is a little drumroll for Sunday. Count them.

Here is the brave thing: today, let someone do something nice for you without trying to repay it immediately. The [[Six of Pentacles]] has been working on you for months. This is the dress rehearsal. Somebody will offer help, a treat, or a compliment. Say yes. Say thank you. Then stop talking, which is the hardest part. The cabin believes in you.
joel.mission: Accept one offer of help today without saying you do not need to, then actually let them help.
joel.omen: A snowdrop or first green shoot poking through dirt. It means something small and brave is about to bloom in you.

reading: The Wood Rat has a secret project: something for Joel's birthday, even if it is only a message. Today the Leo moon makes your creativity bold. Whatever you have planned, make it a little bigger, a little brighter, a little more ridiculous.

Around 4 pm, the light will hit your diamond and throw sparkles across your desk or table. Take that as a sign that whatever you are making is exactly right. You are clever, you see what others miss, and you have been collecting tiny details about Joel all year. Use one. The specific one. He will notice it, and his reaction will be worth everything.
nancy.mission: Write down one small, specific detail you know about Joel that nobody else would remember, and save it for Sunday.
nancy.omen: Sparkles of light thrown by a ring or glass. It means your creative instinct is perfectly on target right now.

together.text: Birthday countdown begins. Each of you name one thing you are brave enough to do this weekend that you would not have done a year ago. Send it in one sentence. The moon is nearly full and keeps track of promises.

title: The Balance Beam Eve
skyStory: The spring equinox arrives this evening: day and night stand exactly equal, like two people sharing a seesaw perfectly. The gibbous moon, ninety-six percent lit, has slid into Virgo and is busy straightening the sky's tablecloth for tomorrow. Everything must be just so. The Fire Tiger's birthday party starts at midnight, and the moon has a clipboard.

reading: The equinox is a door swinging open: light and dark balanced for one breath before the light wins. You were born on this hinge, and tonight it creaks for you. Expect to feel strangely calm, even with ten things in motion.

Spend the evening the way a hinge would: still, steady, letting the door swing. Wear the onyx on your left wrist tonight, the receiving side, and resist the urge to switch it to the right. Tomorrow is about receiving. Practise. The [[Temperance]] card is pouring water between two cups without spilling a drop, and tonight that is you.
joel.mission: Keep the onyx bracelet on your left wrist all evening and do not switch it, no matter how strong the urge.
joel.omen: An egg balancing on its end, a coin landing on its edge, or anything in perfect balance. It means you are ready.

reading: You were born on the solstice, the longest night, and Joel on the equinox, the balance point. Tonight the wheel turns to his day. The mountain holds steady while the fire gets ready to blaze.

There is something you want to send him at midnight, or first thing in the morning. Write it tonight while the equinox light is still in the sky. Be specific. Be warm. Be ridiculous if you want. The [[Six of Swords]] reminds you that he has been helping you row all year. Tomorrow you get to hand him an oar of a different kind: words he will keep.
nancy.mission: Write your birthday message for Joel tonight, read it out loud once to check the rhythm, then schedule it.
nancy.omen: Light and shadow splitting a room exactly in half. It means two forces are perfectly balanced, and good things follow.
nancy.stoneWhy: his receiving stone, held for him

together.text: Equinox night. At sunset, wherever you are, pause for a single breath and think of the other. Light and dark are equal right now, mountain and fire are equal right now. Tomorrow the light wins. Get ready.

title: The Fire Tiger's Full Moon Birthday
skyStory: Spring has arrived, the Fire Tiger turns forty-one, and the full moon rises in Virgo at ninety-nine percent to make it official. Mars throws open every window in the solar system. Saturn, gruff as ever, has baked a lopsided cake and is pretending he did not. The Sun, reborn into Aries, lights forty-one candles in the sky. Even the snowbanks are melting just to make room for the party.

reading: Happy birthday, Fire Tiger. You were born on the hinge of the year, the day the light wins, and today it wins for you. The full moon is shining on your exact birthday for the first time in years, and it brought friends: every star you have ever wished on is back to say they remember.

Today [[The Sun]] card is standing upright for once, no reversal, no lesson, just warm light pouring over you. Your only job is to receive it. Every compliment, every message, every slice of cake. No deflecting. No saying you do not need anything. Switch the onyx to your right wrist at sunset to send that light straight back to Nancy, and watch for the moment she feels it.
joel.mission: Receive every single birthday wish today with only the words thank you, I love that, and let it land.
joel.omen: Forty-one of anything: steps, cars, minutes past the hour. It means the universe is counting with you and cheering.

reading: Today is his day, and you are the co-host. The mountain stands back and lets the fire blaze, which is one of the most generous things a mountain can do. Your ruby will feel warm all day long, like it knows exactly whose birthday it is.

At moonrise, take the ruby off your pinky and set it in the moonlight beside something dark and steady to stand in for his onyx. The Full Moon Recharge. Here is the part you will not believe: at that exact moment, Joel will be switching his onyx to his right wrist, sending light back across the water to you. Don't even scream. The universe planned it, and so, quietly, did you.
nancy.mission: At moonrise, set your ruby in the moonlight for five minutes, then put it back on and text Joel happy birthday, Tiger.
nancy.omen: The full moon caught in bare branches for a moment, then breaking free. The light you two share just got a fresh charge.

together.text: Full Moon Recharge on the birthday equinox. At moonrise, ruby and onyx go into the moonlight together, his wrist switches, her stone glows. Compare the exact minute you each did it. If they match, say DES out loud and laugh until spring arrives completely.

title: Libra Weighs the Leftover Confetti
skyStory: The moon is perfectly full today, one hundred percent, and has drifted into Libra, the sign of the scales. It is weighing what is left from yesterday's party: confetti on one side, gratitude on the other. Gratitude wins easily. Venus, Libra's ruler, sweeps up the glitter and hums. Saturn is having a second slice of the lopsided cake and denying it.

reading: The day after a birthday is a soft landing. The confetti has settled, the messages have slowed, and the cabin is quiet in that satisfied, post-party way. Do not rush back into ten projects. The full moon asks for one more day of glow.

Reread the birthday messages you received. Slowly. Out loud if you are alone. The [[Six of Pentacles]] wants you to notice how much people wanted to give to you, and how good it feels to have received it. Write down the one line that made you grin the hardest and tape it inside a cupboard door. Future-you will open that cupboard on a grey Tuesday and be delighted.
joel.mission: Tape your favourite line from a birthday message inside a cupboard door where you will find it again in a month.
joel.omen: A stray piece of glitter or confetti somewhere it has no business being. It means the celebration is still quietly going on.

reading: You gave a lot yesterday: thought, time, words chosen with care. Today Libra brings the scales back into balance, and it is your turn to rest. The shore is still and silver under the full moon, and the tide has nowhere it needs to be.

Take an hour today that belongs entirely to you. No helping. No levelling anyone up. Just you and something you love, a book, a walk, a hot drink by a window. The Wood Rat curls up in a pile of soft things and closes her eyes, deeply content. The full moon is watching over the shore, keeping the light on so you can rest.
nancy.mission: Claim one full hour today for doing absolutely nothing useful, and defend it like a castle wall.
nancy.omen: The full moon reflected in still water or a window. It means everything is balanced, and you have earned a rest.

together.text: Post-party rest day. Each of you name one tiny, perfect moment from the birthday weekend and send it to the other in a single sentence. Then both of you take the evening off from being useful. Libra insists, and Venus brought blankets.

title: The Scales Tip Toward the Mountain
skyStory: Still full and glowing at ninety-eight percent, the moon lingers in Libra, scales in hand, measuring fairness across the sky. It notices something: the Fire Tiger just got a whole birthday of love, and the Mountain has been giving all winter. Venus raises an eyebrow. Libra adjusts a weight. The scales tip, gently, toward Nancy, and the shore glows a little brighter tonight.

reading: You had your day. Now the scales swing the other way, and the Tiger's best move is to turn all that birthday warmth outward. Today your gift is attention: specific, generous, undivided attention aimed at someone who usually gives it to others.

Send Nancy a message today listing three things she did this winter that made a real difference to you. Be precise. Name the day, the words she used, the moment. The scales want balance, and balance means she gets to hear how much she gives. Then switch the onyx to your right wrist for an hour and send strength across the water. She will feel it.
joel.mission: Switch the onyx to your right wrist for one hour this afternoon and send strength to Nancy across the water.
joel.omen: Two of something perfectly matched, like two mugs or two chairs. It means balance is being restored between you right now.

reading: Libra is tipping the scales your way. Today, receive. Someone will offer help, praise, a small favour, or a long-overdue thank you. The Wood Rat usually spots the gift and quietly hands it to someone else. Not today. Keep it.

Your stacked diamonds catch the moonlight tonight in a little ladder of sparkles, one for every person you helped level up this winter. Count them if you like. The [[Knight of Pentacles]] reversed says stop earning joy and just allow it. You have earned it ten times over already. The mountain can lean back against the sky for one evening and let the light come in.
nancy.mission: When Joel's message arrives today, reply with only thank you and one heart, no deflecting, and mean it.
nancy.omen: A scale, a seesaw or a balanced stack of stones. It means the universe is evening things out in your favour.

together.text: Fairness day. Joel sends three specific thank yous to Nancy. Nancy receives them without arguing. Then, together, pick one small thing to look forward to this spring and say it out loud at the same time over the phone.

title: The Day of the Locked Drawer
skyStory: The waning gibbous moon, ninety-four percent lit, slips into Scorpio, the sign of secrets, keys and deep water. Pluto hands it a ring of old brass keys and points toward a drawer nobody has opened since autumn. The moon jingles the keys thoughtfully. Some drawers hold treasure. Some hold three dried-out pens and a mystery button. Either way, today it gets opened.

reading: Scorpio moons love a mystery, and there is one hiding in your space right now: a box, a folder, a drawer you have avoided because you are not sure what is inside. Today, open it. Spend no more than twenty minutes in there.

You will find one thing worth keeping, one thing worth tossing, and one thing that makes you laugh out loud. The laugh is the real treasure. The Tiger was expecting dread and found a forgotten note, a funny photo, or a gadget whose purpose is lost to history. Keep that one on your desk for a week as a reminder that the scary drawer was never scary.
joel.mission: Open the drawer or box you have been avoiding, give it twenty minutes, and keep the funniest thing you find.
joel.omen: An old key with no known lock. It means something you thought was closed is quietly ready to open.

reading: Scorpio is a detective sign, and the Wood Rat is a natural sleuth. Today you will notice a clue that everyone else has missed: a typo in a document, a pattern in a schedule, a quiet person who needs a hand. Say something. Your eye is sharp as a needle today.

In the evening, a memory surfaces of something you meant to do last autumn and let slip. Do not treat it as guilt. Treat it as a treasure map. The [[Page of Swords]] arrives with a magnifying glass and a pencil behind her ear, asking which clue you would like to follow next. Pick the most fun one. Start tomorrow.
nancy.mission: Spot one mistake or overlooked detail today that nobody else noticed, and point it out kindly and cleverly.
nancy.omen: A magnifying glass, a lens or a reflection showing something hidden. It means your detective instincts are switched on.

together.text: Scorpio treasure hunt. Each of you open one neglected drawer and send the other a description of the strangest thing inside, without naming it. The other must guess what it is in three tries. Prizes are purely imaginary.

title: The Ice Lets Go
skyStory: The waning gibbous moon, eighty-eight percent lit, stays deep in Scorpio, and down on the coast the shore ice finally lets go. It groans, cracks and drifts out with the tide in great white rafts. Pluto, Scorpio's ruler, watches with approval. Letting go is its favourite sport. The moon pulls the tide a little harder tonight, just to help the last stubborn floes on their way.

reading: Something you have been holding tightly, a plan, an expectation, a way things were supposed to go, is ready to drift out with the tide. You will feel it loosen around midday. Do not grab it back. Watch it float.

The Tiger is a hunter, and hunters hate letting prey go. But today the best catch is the one you release. The [[The Hanged Man]] hangs upside down in your path, perfectly calm, seeing everything from a new angle. Try it. Sit somewhere unusual, a step, the floor, the back seat, and look at your week from there. Something you were forcing will suddenly look optional.
joel.mission: Sit somewhere you never sit, like the floor or a stair, for ten minutes and think about your week from there.
joel.omen: Ice sliding off a roof or drifting on water. It means a stuck situation is about to move freely on its own.

reading: This is a shore day in the biggest sense. The ice is leaving, the water is coming back, and you can hear the waves again for the first time since December. You were born on the longest night, and this is the moment the light you promised fully arrives at the water's edge.

If you can, go stand near open water today, even a creek or a puddle catching sky. Let your mother of pearl catch the light. The [[Six of Swords]] is mid-crossing, and today the boat slides out of the ice and into open water. The rowing gets easier from here. You will feel it in your shoulders by evening, a lightness that is new.
nancy.mission: Visit any open water, even a puddle, and drop one small stone or twig in to mark the crossing.
nancy.omen: The sound of water moving where there was only silence. It means the long crossing has reached easier water.

together.text: Ice-out day. Each of you name one thing from this winter you are leaving on the ice as it drifts away. Say it to each other, one sentence each. Then name one thing you want the open water to bring this spring.

title: The Detective Rat Takes a Case
skyStory: The moon, eighty-one percent lit, lingers in Scorpio one more night, wearing a trench coat and a fedora. Someone has misplaced something, and the sky has opened a case file. Pluto is the grumpy police chief. Mercury is the fast-talking informant. And the Wood Rat, unexpectedly, has been hired as the lead detective. The case is small. The drama is enormous.

reading: Today a small object will go missing in your life: a key, a cable, a favourite spoon. It is not lost. It has been borrowed by the Scorpio moon for theatrical purposes. Do not panic. Make a cup of something warm first.

Then, instead of searching, describe the missing thing to Nancy in the most dramatic detective-novel voice you can muster. Her reply, somehow, will tell you exactly where it is. If it does not, the object will turn up on its own around 7 pm, in a place you already checked twice. The cabin finds this extremely funny. Mars is wheezing.
joel.mission: Describe one missing object to Nancy in the voice of a hardboiled detective and ask for her professional opinion.
joel.omen: Something turning up in a place you already checked. It means the universe is playing hide and seek, and you win.

reading: The Wood Rat, famously clever and perceptive, has been appointed chief detective of the solar system for one day only. Your powers of observation are tuned to maximum. You will notice who rearranged the mugs, who moved the stapler, and where everybody's missing things are.

When Joel asks for help finding something, you will know the answer before he finishes the question. Life Path 11 is basically psychic on Scorpio days. Answer with complete confidence, even if you are guessing. You are probably right. If not, at least deliver it with flair. Detectives are judged on style as much as results.
nancy.mission: Solve one small mystery today, a misplaced thing or an unanswered question, and announce the solution like a detective in a drawing room.
nancy.omen: A trench coat, hat or magnifying glass. It means your sleuthing powers are at full strength today.

together.text: Detective day. One of you hides a small object somewhere in your own home and describes the hiding place in a riddle. The other has three guesses. Winner gets to be called Inspector for the rest of the day.

title: The Arrow Lands in the Mud
skyStory: The waning gibbous moon, seventy-three percent lit, moves into Sagittarius and immediately wants an adventure. It fires an arrow toward the horizon, full of optimism. The arrow lands, with a deeply unglamorous squelch, in a big patch of mud. Welcome to mud season. Jupiter, Sagittarius's ruler, laughs so hard its rings wobble. Adventure, it says, always starts a little messy.

reading: Mud season is here, and it is a perfect metaphor for your week: nothing is clean, everything is moving, and the boots are definitely ruined. This is good. Messy movement beats tidy stillness every time. The Tiger does not mind muddy paws.

Something you start today will look clumsy at first. Let it. The first draft of anything looks like an arrow in the mud. The [[Knight of Wands]] rides through puddles without slowing down, because the destination matters more than the splash. Aim at one thing and keep going. By April, the mud will have dried into a path.
joel.mission: Start one thing today badly on purpose, a messy draft or a rough sketch, and refuse to fix it until tomorrow.
joel.omen: Muddy footprints leading somewhere new. It means your messy start is actually headed in exactly the right direction.

reading: Sagittarius moons make everyone want to wander, and you will catch the itch too. Not a big trip. A small one. A new trail, a different coffee shop, a street you have never walked down. The shore is lovely in mud season if you wear the right boots.

Around 1:15 pm a stranger will ask you for directions, or you will overhear someone describing a place you have never been. Take note. That is the Sagittarius moon slipping you an invitation. Your onyx bracelet will feel extra steady on your wrist, reminding you that wandering is safe when you have strong roots. Go see something new.
nancy.mission: Walk down one street, trail or hallway you have never explored, and find one thing worth telling Joel about.
nancy.omen: A stranger asking for directions. It means an adventure is knocking, and you are invited.

together.text: Mud season expedition. Each of you go somewhere new, even tiny, and send the other a photo of your muddiest boot or step. The muddiest photo is declared the bravest explorer. Jupiter is the official judge and loves a mess.

title: The Day of the Twin Robins
skyStory: The last quarter moon, sixty-three percent lit, sits in Sagittarius with a pair of binoculars, watching for the first robins of spring. Jupiter has placed a bet with Saturn: two robins, two places, same minute. Saturn scoffs. The moon grins. Somewhere over the woods between the cabin and the shore, two little red-breasted birds are already flying in opposite directions.

reading: Today, a robin will land near the cabin, probably on a fence, a branch or a patch of thawed grass. You will notice it around 8:20 in the morning. It will look at you with that sideways robin look, like it has news.

At the very same minute, Nancy is seeing a robin too. You will find out when you compare notes later, and you will both stop mid-sentence. Don't even scream. It is the first robin of spring, delivered in a matching pair, one to the cabin and one to the shore. The [[Two of Cups]] is raising a toast to the fact that you two keep seeing the same things.
joel.mission: Note the exact minute you see your first robin today and send it to Nancy without saying anything else.
joel.omen: A robin pulling a worm from thawed ground. It means spring has officially arrived at the cabin, and so has good news.
joel.stoneWhy: her stone, steady as a perch

reading: The Wood Rat hears the robin before she sees it, that bright, bubbling morning song after a long winter of silence. Look out the window around 8:20 am. There it is, puffed up, important, completely sure of itself.

When Joel texts you a time later today, look at the minute. It will match yours. ΔΕΣ. The universe sent one robin to the cabin and one to the shore at the same moment, just to prove the thread between you is still pulled tight. Tell the story tonight with full wing gestures. Your hands have been waiting all winter for a bird to act out.
nancy.mission: Act out a robin landing, wings and all, for someone today, and tell them the matching robin story.
nancy.omen: A robin singing from a high branch. It means two people far apart are hearing the same song at the same time.

together.text: First robin day. Each of you write down the exact minute you saw your first robin and swap. If they match, or even land close, say DES and add a robin to the year's list of evidence. Jupiter wins the bet with Saturn.

title: The Mountain Gets Its Moon Back
skyStory: The last quarter moon, fifty-four percent lit, returns to Capricorn, Nancy's sign, for the second time this month. Saturn hears it coming up the trail and puts the kettle back on, delighted. They pick up their conversation right where they left it on the second, except now the snow is melting and the mountain has more to say. Mars, again, was not invited. He brought cookies anyway.

reading: The moon is visiting the mountain again, and this time you have something to bring. Think back to the second of March, when the moon first passed through Capricorn. What has changed since then? Something has. Probably more than you think.

Today, offer Nancy a piece of help she did not ask for but will love: a link, a joke, an idea, a piece of encouragement that fits her current project exactly. The Tiger knows her well enough by now to aim precisely. Keep it small and specific. The best gifts are the ones that say I noticed what you are working on. She will grin at her screen.
joel.mission: Send Nancy one small, specific thing that helps her current project, without asking whether she wants it first.
joel.omen: A goat, a peak or a stone wall printed somewhere nearby. That is the mountain saying it is ready for your gift.

reading: The moon is home with you again, and the mountain feels strong, steady and very much in charge. Saturn has rearranged your afternoon so that one hard task flows unusually easily. Watch for it. It will feel like the work is doing itself.

Use the home advantage to finish something you started at the beginning of the month. You have had four weeks of patience, and today the patience pays out. The [[Six of Swords]] shows the boat nearly at the far bank. One more stroke. Then step out onto the shore, look back at how far you came, and let yourself be impressed.
nancy.mission: Finish one task you started back at the beginning of March, then look back at your first note about it.
nancy.omen: A mountain peak, real or painted, catching the light. It means your steady climb is nearly at the top.

together.text: The moon is back in Capricorn. Each of you name one thing that is different now from March 2. Send it in one sentence. Saturn will add both answers to the cozy ledger he keeps by the kettle.

title: The Day of the Patient Crocus
skyStory: The last quarter moon, forty-five percent lit, rests in Capricorn, taking its time. Down below, in a muddy garden bed, a single purple crocus has decided to open. It waited all winter for this exact afternoon. Saturn admires its discipline. Venus admires its colour. The moon admires its sense of timing and makes a note to try that sometime.

reading: There is a crocus somewhere near you, about to open. It waited months, under snow and ice, for exactly the right moment. You are waiting on something too, and today is a good day to realize the waiting has been doing quiet work underground.

Do something to celebrate a small thing that finally arrived after a long wait. A package, a reply, a warm day, a finished project. Make it a feast: your favourite meal, a candle at dinner, music while you cook. The [[Knight of Pentacles]] reversed says do not wait for a big reason. A crocus is reason enough. Joy does not need permission.
joel.mission: Celebrate one small, long-awaited thing tonight with a candle at dinner and a toast said out loud to it.
joel.omen: A crocus or any purple flower in the mud. It means something you waited patiently for is finally here.

reading: The shore smells like spring today: salt, mud, wet wood and something green. The tide is coming back to the beach in long, slow sighs. You were born on the darkest day to promise that the light would return. Look around. It has.

Tonight, have a small feast for no reason. Lay the table like it is a holiday. Light something. Play music. Tell a story at dinner with all ten fingers dancing. The Wood Rat knows celebration is not a reward for finishing; it is fuel for continuing. Joel is doing the same thing tonight at the cabin. Raise a glass toward the woods.
nancy.mission: Set the table tonight like it is a holiday dinner, for no reason at all, and light one candle.
nancy.omen: The first green shoots along the shoreline grass. It means the light you promised has arrived, right on schedule.

together.text: Crocus feast night. Both of you lay a fancy table for no reason and send each other a photo of it. Raise a glass at 7 pm sharp toward each other's direction, toasting to the long wait being over.

title: March Leaves Like a Lamb
skyStory: The waning moon, thirty-five percent lit, sits quietly in Capricorn for the last night of March. The month came in like a lion and is leaving like a very sleepy lamb, curled up in a patch of new grass. Saturn tucks a blanket over it. Mars, for once, is quiet. The equinox has passed, the birthday is done, and April is waiting at the door, holding flowers.

reading: Last day of the month: time to look back at the new moon intention you hid inside a book on the sixth. Find it. Read it. You may be surprised. The Tiger carried that one log further than you thought.

Whatever happened with it, celebrate the attempt. The [[Knight of Wands]] did not win every race, but he rode every one with his whole heart. Write a new single sentence for April and tuck it back into the same book. Then close the book, close March, and walk outside to smell the mud. Spring is here. You helped bring it.
joel.mission: Find the intention you hid on March 6, read it aloud, then write a fresh one for April in the same book.
joel.omen: A lamb, sheep or anything woolly and calm. It means the month ended gently, and April will start well.
joel.stoneWhy: stack March on top of April

reading: The last night of March, and the moon is in your sign, keeping you company as the month closes. Look back at the tiny map you drew under the new moon, two dots: where you were, where you were heading. You moved. You definitely moved.

Draw a new map for April. Same rules: two dots, one line between. The [[Six of Swords]] is still mid-crossing, but the water is open now, the ice is gone, the robins are back. The rowing feels lighter. Joel is still rowing beside you. Put the map somewhere secret, and let April surprise you.
nancy.mission: Draw April's tiny map, two dots and one line, and tuck it next to March's map in your secret spot.
nancy.omen: Wind blowing gently from the south. It means the next month brings warmer things, and you are ready for them.

together.text: End-of-March crossing. Each of you send the other one word that sums up this month, and one word for what you want April to be. No explanations. Just two words each, like stepping stones over the creek.
